feeds.title: Castle Studies Trust Blog
feeds.description: The Castle Studies Trust is a UK-based charity founded in 2012 with the mission of increasing knowledge of castles in the UK and abroad. The key focus is on sites not in the care of major heritage organizations. Castle Studies Trust Blog gives an advanced understanding of castles.

feeds.title: Norwich Castle Museum & Art Gallery
feeds.description: Norwich Castle Museum & Art Gallery is packed with treasures to inspire and intrigue visitors of all ages. One of the city's most famous landmarks, it was built by the Normans as a Royal Palace 900 years ago. Now a museum and art gallery, it is home to some of the most outstanding collections of fine art, archaeology, and natural history.

feeds.title: Dundas Castle Blog
feeds.description: Dundas Castle in Edinburgh is the most spectacular venue for your event. Whether it is a wedding, a corporate event, or a family celebration, the variety of buildings, impressive rooms, and 17 bedrooms all 'under one roof' will provide you with a stay that is truly unique.

feeds.title: Visit European Castles Blog
feeds.description: At Visit European Castles, we want to make it easier for you to find the best historic castles, palaces, and stately homes in Europe. Our travel guides help you find the best castles in the city, region, or country that you are going to visit. Whether you are looking for a specific destination that you are going to visit or if you are looking for something specific like an architectural style. We're here to help.

feeds.title: Newcastle Castle Blog
feeds.description: Newcastle Castle is where the story of Newcastle began and the reason it got its name. Steeped in history, this imposing Norman fortress is a rugged reminder of northern England's turbulent past. Discover the most commanding views across the city and the River Tyne. The quintessential view of Newcastle and Gateshead.

feeds.title: Balintore Castle Restoration Project
feeds.description: Balintore Castle is a wonderful place both in architecture and its surroundings. Read the blog to get the latest news and announcements on Balintore Castle Restoration Project as well as blog, offers and about know about the history of the castle.

feeds.title: Confessions of a Castleholic
feeds.description: Hi, my name is Svenja and I'm a Castleholic. And this is Confessions of a Castleholic, my website dedicated to the beauty and splendor of the world's castles and palaces. I share my experiences, their history, and plenty of pictures from my visits to the wonderful sights in Germany, Europe, and all around the world.

feeds.title: Castrum to Castle Blog
feeds.description: We create informative articles about castles and famous historical figures such as kings and queens. We also provide all the visiting information you need to help plan your visit to each castle. Explore Information about new castles that are updated regularly.

feeds.title: Edinburgh Castle Blog
feeds.description: Edinburgh Castle is one of the most exciting historic sites in Western Europe. Set in the heart of Scotland's dynamic capital city, it is sure to capture your imagination. The scenery will take your breath away. There are many ways to experience Edinburgh Castle. Explore the blog where you will find an itinerary, and an audio guide to show you around.

feeds.title: Kilkenny Castle Blog
feeds.description: Kilkenny Castle is open to visitors all year round and is largely a Victorian remodeling of the thirteenth-century defensive Castle. Each year, hundreds of thousands of visitors come to see this grand country house and walk through its fifty acres of rolling parkland with mature trees and an abundance of wildlife. Other features include a formal terraced rose garden, woodlands, and a man-made lake, which were added in the nineteenth century.

feeds.title: Historic Environment Scotland Blog » Stirling Castle
feeds.description: We are here to safeguard the nation's historic environment and promote its understanding and enjoyment for present and future generations. We care for properties in every part of Scotland and they range from standing stones and brochs to abbeys and cathedrals. We have a tremendously skilled staff - ranging from archaeologists, art historians, conservators, and craftsmen, to guides, custodians, and key keepers.
